sections.title: Sound of the letter
paragraphs: The letter (effe) /ɛf/ makes the sound /f/ in the word (film) /film/, which means film, movie. This letter can produce two spoken sounds, and sometimes it stays silent.

sections.title: How to say it
paragraphs: To make the first sound, place your top teeth on your bottom lip. Blow air gently between them without using your voice. To make the second sound, keep the same mouth shape. Add your voice so you feel a strong buzz on your throat.

sections.title: Spelling rules
paragraphs: In most positions, the letter sounds like the sound /f/, as in the word (café) /ka.fe/. When the number nine links to a word starting with a vowel, the letter sounds like the sound /v/, as in (neuf ans) /nœ.vɑ̃/. In a few special words, the letter is not pronounced, as in (clef) /kle/.

sections.title: Comparing with English
paragraphs: The main sound is identical to the English sound in fox. No special adjustment is needed. When you voice the letter before a vowel, make sure it matches the English sound in vine. Simply let your vocal cords buzz.
